title: ACT ON ACQUISITION AND MANAGEMENT OF COAST GUARD EQUIPMENT
title_original: 해양경찰장비 도입 및 관리에 관한 법률
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to contribute to safeguarding sovereignty, maintaining public order, and ensuring safety and other relevant interests at sea, by prescribing fundamental matters regarding the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
  1. The term “coast guard equipment” means vessels, aircraft, and onboard equipment necessary for performing the duties of the coast guard under Article 14 of the Coast Guard Act;
  2. The term “onboard equipment” means equipment installed on and used in vessels or aircraft, as prescribed by Presidential Decree;
  3. The term “acquisition” means purchasing, constructing, or manufacturing coast guard equipment and delivering such equipment to a coast guard equipment manager;
  4. The term “management” means acts such as inspection, maintenance, and disposal conducted by a coast guard equipment manager upon taking delivery of coast guard equipment, to ensure that such equipment can perform its original functions;
  5. The term “operation” means the safe use of coast guard equipment in accordance with its functions and purposes;
  6. The term “disposal” means the transfer of ownership of coast guard equipment to a person other than the State, or the transfer of management rights to another agency, by means such as sale or gratuitous transfer;
  7. The term “service life” means the economically useful life of coast guard equipment, estimated as the period during which such equipment can properly perform coast guard duties without operational impairment;
  8. The term “coast guard equipment manager” means a public official of the Korea Coast Guard who directly manages and operates coast guard equipment.

Article 3 (Relationship to other statutes) Except as otherwise provided in other statutes, the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment and other relevant matters shall be governed by this Act.

CHAPTER II FORMULATION OF MASTER PLANS FOR ACQUISITION AND MANAGEMENT OF COAST GUARD EQUIPMENT

Article 4 (Formulation of master plans for acquisition and management of coast guard equipment) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall formulate and implement a master plan for the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment (hereinafter referred to as "master plan") every 5 years to efficiently perform the duties of the coast guard.
  (2) A master plan shall include the following:
  1. Mid- to long-term policy objectives and directions for the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment;
  2. Mid- to long-term implementation objectives for the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment;
  3. Securing financial resources for the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment;
  4. Establishment and improvement of systems for the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment;
  5. Technological innovation and practical application of coast guard equipment;
  6. Expansion of infrastructure related to the management of coast guard equipment;
  7. Training of personnel for the operation and maintenance of coast guard equipment;
  8. Other matters necessary for the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment.
  (3) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall formulate and implement an implementation plan for the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment (hereinafter referred to as "implementation plan") each year to efficiently implement the master plan.
  (4) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall submit a master plan and an implementation plan formulated under paragraphs (1) and (3) to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly. The same shall also apply to any modification of important matters prescribed by Presidential Decree in the formulated master plan or implementation plan.
  (5) Matters necessary for the formulation, implementation, etc. of master plans and implementation plans shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 5 (Securing of financial resources for acquisition and management of coast guard equipment) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall prepare measures to continuously and stably secure the financial resources necessary to effectively promote the acquisition, management, etc. of coast guard equipment, in accordance with the relevant master plan and implementation plan.

Article 6 (Fact-finding surveys) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may conduct a fact-finding survey on the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment for the formulation and implementation of a master plan and an implementation plan.
  (2) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may request manufacturers or sellers of coast guard equipment, or the heads of institutions related to the acquisition and management of coast guard equipment, to submit materials necessary for a fact-finding survey. In such cases, a person so requested shall comply the request unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.
  (3) The scope, methods, and other matters necessary for fact-finding surveys under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 7 (Research and development of coast guard equipment and promotion of related industries) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may establish and promote policy measures necessary for the research and development of coast guard equipment and the promotion and development of related industries, in order to ensure the performance of such equipment and enhance operational capabilities.
  (2) To efficiently promote research and development projects for coast guard equipment, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may conduct such projects with any of the following institutions, organizations, etc.:
  1. National and public research institutes;
  2. Colleges and universities, industrial colleges, junior colleges, and technical colleges under the Higher Education Act;
  3. Government-funded science and technology research institutes established under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutes;
  4. Business-affiliated research institutes or dedicated research and development departments recognized under Article 14-2 (1) of the Basic Research Promotion and Technology Development Support Act;
  5. Corporations established under the Civil Act or other statutes, which are research institutes or corporation-affiliated research institutes in the field of public security;
  6. Specific research institutes under Article 2 of the Specific Research Institutes Support Act;
  7. Other institutions or organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree, which conduct research, survey, technological development, etc. in the relevant fields.
  (3) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may conduct the following projects for the promotion and support of industries related to coast guard equipment:
  1. Matters regarding international cooperation for technological development and technical support related to coast guard equipment;
  2. The organization and operation of exhibitions and academic conferences related to coast guard equipment.
  (4) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may fully or partially provide subsidies to cover necessary expenses incurred in conducting projects under paragraph (2) or (3).

Article 8 (Training of professional personnel) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may establish and implement policy measures necessary for the development of professional personnel and the improvement of technology related to coast guard equipment.
  (2) To train professional personnel under paragraph (1), the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may designate a university or college under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act, a specific research institute under Article 2 of the Specific Research Institutes Support Act, or a research institute, institution, or organization related to coast guard equipment as a professional personnel training institution and may have such entity provide the necessary education and training.
  (3) If a professional personnel training institution designated under paragraph (2) falls under any of the following categories, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may revoke its designation or may order the full or partial suspension of its business operations for a specified period of up to 6 months; provided, the designation shall be revoked in the case of subparagraph 1:
  1. Where the institution has obtained the designation by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where the institution fails to perform the duties under paragraph (2) without good cause;
  3. Where it is deemed impracticable for the institution to continue performing the duties under paragraph (2).
  (4) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may, within the budget, fully or partially subsidize a professional personnel training institution designated under paragraph (2) to cover the expenses incurred in providing education and training.
  (5) Other matters necessary for the standards for designating professional personnel training institutions and the procedures for revoking such designation and suspending designated duties, and other relevant details shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER III ACQUISITION OF COAST GUARD EQUIPMENT

Article 9 (Basic principles for acquisition of coast guard equipment) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may acquire coast guard equipment considering the following principles:
  1. Ensuring transparency and efficiency in coast guard equipment acquisition projects;
  2. Acquiring excellent equipment utilizing the latest technology;
  3. Enhancing the operability of coast guard equipment by ensuring interoperability between equipment;
  4. Collecting sufficient opinions from coast guard equipment managers and experts.

Article 10 (Special cases regarding contracts) (1) When the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard concludes a contract for the acquisition of coast guard vessels or aircraft used for maritime security operations under the United Defense Act, if it is deemed necessary to make advance or interim payments due to the nature of the contract, such payments may be made within the budgeted amount for the relevant year, notwithstanding the provisions of the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party and other related statutes or regulations; provided, any advance or interim payments made must not be used for purposes other than the fulfillment of the relevant contract.
  (2) The standards, methods, and procedures for the payment of advance and interim payments under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. In such cases, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall have a prior consultation with the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 11 (Selection of critical onboard equipment) (1) When acquiring vessels or aircraft, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may select onboard equipment that significantly affects the performance of the equipment (hereinafter referred to as "critical onboard equipment") and require its installation.
  (2) When acquiring coast guard equipment of the same performance and type, the use of critical onboard equipment selected under paragraph (1) may be considered.
  (3) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures for selecting critical onboard equipment shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

CHAPTER IV MANAGEMENT OF COAST GUARD EQUIPMENT

Article 12 (Record and management of coast guard equipment) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall record and manage matters regarding the status and management of coast guard equipment in possession, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
  (2) When entering matters regarding the status and management of coast guard equipment into a computerized system, such entries may serve in place of separate written records.

Article 13 (Service life of coast guard equipment) (1) The service life of coast guard equipment shall be determined by the Administrator of the Public Procurement Service under Article 16-2 (1) of the Commodity Management Act; provided, for coast guard equipment whose service life is not determined by the Administrator or which is not subject to the application of that Act, the service life may be otherwise determined by the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard. In such cases, the relevant details shall be notified to the Administrator.
  (2) If special circumstances make it impracticable to apply the service life determined by the Administrator of the Public Procurement Service Article 16-2 (1) of the Commodity Management Act, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may adjust the service life, in consultation with the Administrator.

Article 14 (Safety assessment of coast guard equipment) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may conduct a safety assessment for vessels that have exceeded their service life under Article 13, taking into account factors, such as the construction period, performance, and operational conditions of the relevant vessels, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Decommissioning of coast guard equipment) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall decommission coast guard equipment under Article 40 of the State Property Act if it is deemed impracticable to secure the minimum performance and safety of the relevant equipment, based on the results of the safety assessment under Article 14 or due to an accident or malfunction.

Article 16 (Disposal of decommissioned coast guard equipment) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall, with respect to coast guard equipment decommissioned under Article 15, seek opinions from the heads of central government agencies, etc. defined in subparagraph 11 of Article 2 of the State Property Act, for opinions on the administrative conversion of such equipment under Article 16 of that Act.
  (2) Notwithstanding the request for opinions under paragraph (1), if no opinion is presented regarding the administrative conversion, the decommissioned coast guard equipment may be sold under Article 48 of the State Property Act.
  (3) Coast guard equipment shall, in principle, be dismantled before sale under paragraph (2); provided, it need not be dismantled when sold overseas for the purpose of promoting international friendship or when sold to a local government or public organization for nonprofit public purposes.

Article 17 (Gratuitous transfer of coast guard equipment) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may gratuitously transfer decommissioned coast guard equipment to a developing country defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Framework Act on International Development Cooperation to promote international cooperation, notwithstanding Article 16 of this Act and Article 55 of the State Property Act.
  (2) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may perform maintenance, etc. necessary to preserve the performance of coast guard equipment that has been decided to be gratuitously transferred under paragraph (1).
  (3) Matters necessary for the standards, procedures, etc. for selecting countries eligible for gratuitous transfer under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Education and training for coast guard equipment managers) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall establish and implement policy measures regarding the education and training of coast guard equipment managers, in order to efficiently manage and operate coast guard equipment and to enhance the capabilities of such managers.
  (2) Coast guard equipment managers shall receive education and training conducted by the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard in order to acquire the skills and knowledge necessary for the management and operation of coast guard equipment, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) To enhance the expertise and capabilities of coast guard equipment managers, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may have an institution or organization designated by the Commissioner General conduct the education and training under paragraph (2) on his or her behalf.
  (4) Matters necessary for the details, duration, and other relevant aspects of education and training for coast guard equipment managers shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Operation of supervisors) (1) When designing, constructing, or repairing vessels, or manufacturing, purchasing, or repairing aircraft, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may designate and assign a supervisor to the relevant design, construction, repair, or manufacturing company for the purpose of process management and performance assurance and for other relevant purposes.
  (2) A supervisor under paragraph (1) shall be appointed from among public officials of the Korea Coast Guard, who meet the qualifications prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Matters necessary for the standards and methods for assignment, operation, and other relevant aspects of supervisors shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

CHAPTER V MARKING OF COAST GUARD EQUIPMENT

Article 20 (Painting and marking of coast guard equipment) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall paint and mark the exterior of coast guard equipment so that it can be identified as equipment necessary for performing the duties of the Korea Coast Guard.
  (2) Matters regarding the painting and marking of coast guard equipment shall be determined by the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard.
  (3) No painting or marking under paragraph (1) shall be applied to vessels or aircraft other than those owned or used by the Korea Coast Guard and its affiliated agencies; provided, vessels and aircraft that support coast guard operations, such as maritime safety management and search and rescue activities, may be used after obtaining approval from the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 21 (Installation of warning lights) (1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may install warning lights on coast guard equipment.
  (2) No person shall install warning lights under paragraph (1) on vessels that are not coast guard equipment; provided, this shall not apply to vessels operated by public institutions.
  (3) Matters necessary for the standards for the installation of warning lights under paragraph (1) and other relevant details shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

CHAPTER VI SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 22 (Hearings) To revoke the designation of a professional personnel training institution or suspend its designated tasks under Article 8 (3), the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall hold a hearing.

Article 23 (Delegation of authority) Part of the authority of the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard under this Act may be delegated to the head of its affiliated agency, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 24 (Administrative fines) (1) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine of up to 5 million won:
  1. A person who applies painting and marking, or similar painting and marking, in violation of Article 20 (3);
  2. A person who installs warning lights on a vessel, in violation of Article 21 (2).
  (2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
